text.p: Italian debt instruments staged a late recovery after a roller-coaster session and weaker start, helped by firmer U.S. Treasuries on a raft of positive economic data, traders said.
News that President Yeltsin sacked his security chief Alexander Lebed cast a shadow over German markets and bunds erased earlier gains, but other bond markets gained.

The lira firmed against an easier mark and a stronger dollar. Traders said Milan had partly absorbed losses seen on Wednesday and was now more optimistic about fundamentals, looking ahead to preliminary October CPI data out next week.
